problem_severity_frequency.rationale: The obligation is dated, primary-evidenced and recurring (monthly payroll from 2027-04-06), but buyer-felt severity is undemonstrated: voluntary payrolling has supported per-period BiK values for years, and no employer/bureau pain or failed workaround is cited. Mandate is market context, not demand. Cap: problem asserted without buyer-side evidence => max 2.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer hypothesis (SME finance/payroll or bureau principal) is identifiable but no budget owner, budget line or comparable existing spend is evidenced. ADP/Saffery recommendations are advisory content, which is not demand.

evidence_strength.rationale: Strong dated primary sources (HMRC policy paper, SI 2026/189) corroborated by ATT/CIOT/ICAEW and vendor commentary. Adequate for the market/regulatory facts, but no primary evidence about buyer behaviour, incumbents or willingness to pay.

distribution.rationale: Channels (bureau networks, accountant/payroll communities, software marketplaces) are plausible but untested with no prospects. Cap: channel plausible, no prospects => max 2.

differentiation.rationale: Wedge is contested: the seam has existed under voluntary payrolling since 2016 and payroll vendors are building the adjacent RTI fields; no cited incumbent already ingests provider data, but the data owners can self-supply. Cap: incumbent/adjacent contest => max 2.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: Decisive disconfirmation available in ≤3 days at £0 via a desk capability scan with pre-fixed thresholds; a WTP test is also cheap (≤20 human-hours) once the scan survives.

feasibility.rationale: Ingestion/normalisation of provider exports into payroll import formats is ordinary integration work; the hard part is provider cooperation and per-product formats, not novel technology.

economics.rationale: Pricing and margin are modelled assumptions on untested inputs; if provider data must be chased manually the business is services-like and thin. Cap: modelled economics on untested inputs => max 2, low confidence.

founder_fit.rationale: No evidence recorded on founder fit.

risk.rationale: Handles payroll and medical-benefit personal data (privacy/trust exposure, DPIA and security needed) and depends on payroll-vendor import formats and provider cooperation; no regulated activity identified. Manageable but not yet mitigated.

economic_buyer.note: Buyer hypothesis exists but no budget owner or comparable spend is evidenced.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Bureau/employer interviews confirming who owns the budget and what they spend today on P11D/benefit administration.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Obligation is recurring and dated; buyer-felt pain and willingness to pay are unproven.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Willingness-to-pay test (escalation experiment) after the capability scan survives.

non_paid_distribution.note: Bureau/accountant channels plausible; no prospects or channel tests.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Channel test: measure whether bureaus/accountant networks engage without paid acquisition.

defensible_wedge.note: Incumbent bridge exists: Zhoosh Benefits ingests benefit changes and emits per-period taxable payroll reports for the exact medical-benefit seam (page dated 2026-08-04), with The Electric Car Scheme (API/SFTP monthly payroll inputs) and Zest (provider integrations) as further named platforms; Zellis/Benefex and IRIS's managed service add enterprise/managed paths. Precommitted scan rule: >=2 platforms already ingest provider BiK data => fail.

no_network_effects_needed.note: Single-sided ingestion tool; value does not depend on other users joining.

plausible_margins.note: Software margin only if ingestion is automated; services burden if providers must be chased.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Build/desk estimate of automation coverage plus pilot unit economics.

acceptable_risk.note: Payroll and medical-benefit personal data; privacy/trust and platform-dependency risk not yet assessed.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: DPIA and security review before any pilot; confirm no regulated activity.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: Desk-only capability scan with pre-fixed kill thresholds: GBP 0, <=6 human-hours, <=3 calendar days.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability currently requires several independent optimistic assumptions (providers do not self-supply, vendors do not bundle, buyers pay, channel works).
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: Capability scan, then willingness-to-pay test; re-score if any optimistic assumption fails.

history.reason: Independent false-negative audit (ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol) approved the kill (kill upheld). The scan met its precommitted falsification threshold; vendor evidence does not prove share, and a small-employer segment must not be promoted without separate evidence. Reopening condition recorded in the response file.
